claims.claim: US long-term care readily runs into six figures a year: the 2024 national median for a semi-private nursing home room was $111,325 and a private room $127,750.
claims.episode_span: keeping an aging parent at home or in a facility runs into six figures a year once round-the-clock assistance begins
claims.source_title: Genworth and CareScout Release Cost of Care Survey Results for 2024
claims.supporting_quote: The national annual median cost of a semi-private room in a nursing home rose to $111,325, an increase of 7%, while the cost of a private room in a nursing home increased 9% to $127,750.

claims.claim: The 2024 national median annual cost of a home health aide was $77,792.
claims.episode_span: The result is that a typical private-pay assisted-living unit or full-time home-care arrangement lands in the range of roughly eighty to one hundred fifty thousand dollars annually in most U.S. regions.
claims.source_title: Genworth and CareScout Release Cost of Care Survey Results for 2024
claims.supporting_quote: personal assistance with activities such as bathing, dressing, and eating, has increased 3% to an annual median cost of $77,792

claims.claim: Direct care work has high turnover and churn, driven by low wages, insufficient hours, limited benefits, and high workplace injury rates.
claims.episode_span: the data on turnover already shows that aides themselves change frequently, so the continuity families value is already fragile under the present model
claims.source_title: Why Do Direct Care Workers Leave Their Jobs, and Where Do They Seek Work Next? - PHI
claims.supporting_quote: Low wages, insufficient hours, limited benefits, high workplace injury rates, and many other precarious working conditions lead to high rates of turnover and churn in the U.S. direct care workforce.

claims.claim: Manual patient handling and heavy manual lifting during transfers and repositioning are a major source of musculoskeletal injuries among care workers.
claims.episode_span: one-on-one or two-on-one staffing is required for transfers and falls prevention because manual lifting limits and liability rules have not been widely displaced by mechanical aids
claims.source_title: Safe Patient Handling | Occupational Safety and Health Administration
claims.supporting_quote: These injuries are due in large part to overexertion related to repeated manual patient handling activities, often involving heavy manual lifting associated with transferring, and repositioning patients and working in extremely awkward postures.

claims.claim: Assistive patient-handling equipment (lifts and transfer devices) benefits both care staff and the people being moved.
claims.episode_span: Ceiling lifts, sit-to-stand devices, and powered wheelchairs already exist; wider adoption hinges on reimbursement rules and facility retrofit costs rather than new invention.
claims.source_title: Safe Patient Handling | Occupational Safety and Health Administration
claims.supporting_quote: The use of assistive patient handling equipment and devices is beneficial not only for healthcare staff, but also for patients.

claims.claim: Many falls among older adults can be prevented through exercise, medication management, vision checks, and home-safety changes.
claims.episode_span: Strength and balance programs, medication reconciliation, and nutrition support have documented effects on fall rates and hospital admissions
claims.source_title: Falls and Fractures in Older Adults: Causes and Prevention | National Institute on Aging
claims.supporting_quote: However, many falls can be prevented. For example, exercising, managing your medications, having your vision checked, and making your home safer are all steps you can take to prevent a fall.
